questions.question_english: Under Section 33(7) of the POCSO Act, 2012, during trial proceedings before the Special Court, whose statutory duty is it to ensure that the child is not exposed in any way to the accused?
options_english: The Public Prosecutor
The Special Court
The Investigating Police Officer

questions.explanation_english: Under Section 33(7) of the POCSO Act, 2012, the statutory duty is explicitly placed upon 'The Special Court'. The section mandates: 'The Special Court shall ensure that the child is not exposed in any way to the accused at the time of recording of the evidence, while at the same time ensuring that the accused is in a position to hear the statement of the child and communicate with his advocate to prepare his defence, by having single visibility mirrors or curtains or by any other device.' This critical provision balances the constitutional rights of fair trial and defence representation for the accused with the paramount statutory objective of protecting child victims from secondary victimization, intimidation, and trauma in the courtroom. Principals and support persons accompanying student witnesses to court should be cognizant of this protective courtroom architecture.

सही उत्तर B (विशेष न्यायालय - The Special Court) है।

1. एकतरफा दृश्य दर्पण (Single visibility mirrors), पर्दे (Curtains) या वीडियो कॉन्फ्रेंसिंग जैसे उपकरणों की व्यवस्था करता है।

questions.question_english: A School Principal is officially informed by the Special Juvenile Police Unit (SJPU) that an FIR under the POCSO Act has been registered against a senior PGT teacher based on an alleged outside-school incident. What is the Principal's immediate administrative responsibility?
options_english: Do nothing at all since the alleged incident occurred outside school premises
Immediately report to the Directorate of Education / Competent Authority for placing the teacher under suspension
Conduct an independent internal school inquiry to examine evidence and prove the teacher's innocence
Force the accused teacher to submit a voluntary resignation or take compulsory retirement
questions.explanation_english: When a criminal case under the POCSO Act is registered against an educational employee, the safety of students and institutional integrity are paramount. Under statutory service codes (such as Central Civil Services (Classification, Control and Appeal) Rules, 1965 or relevant State Education Service Rules), facing criminal prosecution for serious offences involving moral turpitude warrants immediate disciplinary action. The Principal, as Head of Institution, must immediately report the registration of the FIR to the Directorate of Education or the Competent Disciplinary Authority recommending that the teacher be placed under immediate suspension. The Principal cannot overlook the matter simply because the incident occurred off-campus, nor can the Principal conduct a parallel internal inquiry or unilaterally force resignation/retirement. Suspension ensures the teacher has no access to students while criminal and departmental processes run their legal course.
questions.explanation_hindi: यदि किसी विद्यालय शिक्षक के विरुद्ध बाल यौन उत्पीड़न जैसे गंभीर अपराध में पॉक्सो अधिनियम के तहत प्राथमिकी (FIR) दर्ज होती है, तो छात्रों की सुरक्षा और विद्यालय की शुचिता सर्वोच्च प्राथमिकता होती है। केंद्रीय सिविल सेवा (वर्गीकरण, नियंत्रण एवं अपील) नियमावली, 1965 तथा शिक्षा सेवा नियमावलियों के तहत गंभीर आपराधिक मामलों में संलिप्त कर्मचारी को सेवा से दूर रखने हेतु तत्काल निलंबन (Suspension) का प्रावधान है। विद्यालय के प्राचार्य का तात्कालिक प्रशासनिक कर्तव्य है कि वह घटना की जानकारी तुरंत शिक्षा निदेशालय अथवा सक्षम अनुशासनिक प्राधिकारी को दे और शिक्षक के निलंबन की अनुशंसा करे। प्राचार्य न तो परिसर से बाहर की घटना कहकर इसे नजरअंदाज कर सकते हैं, न ही उन्हें समानांतर जांच करने या त्यागपत्र देने के लिए बाध्य करने का अधिकार है। अतः विकल्प B सही उत्तर है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) Report to Directorate of Education for placing teacher under suspension

questions.question_english: Under the amended POCSO Act, what is the minimum mandatory term of imprisonment for committing penetrative sexual assault on a child below 12 years of age?
options_english: 7 years rigorous imprisonment
10 years rigorous imprisonment
20 years rigorous imprisonment
Life imprisonment without parole
questions.explanation_english: Following the POCSO (Amendment) Act, 2019 (Act 25 of 2019), Section 5(m) and Section 6(1) were substantially amended to provide stringent deterrence against heinous crimes on young children. Under Section 5(m), committing penetrative sexual assault on a child below 12 years of age is classified as 'aggravated penetrative sexual assault'. Section 6(1) provides that whoever commits aggravated penetrative sexual assault on a child below twelve years of age shall be punished with rigorous imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than twenty years, but which may extend to imprisonment for life (which shall mean imprisonment for the remainder of that person's natural life), or with death, and shall also be liable to fine. Prior to the 2019 amendment, the minimum punishment for aggravated penetrative sexual assault was 10 years, which was enhanced to 20 years to reinforce protection for children below 12 years.
questions.explanation_hindi:
सही उत्तर C (20 वर्ष का कठोर कारावास) है।

पॉक्सो (संशोधन) अधिनियम, 2019 के माध्यम से धारा 5(m) तथा धारा 6(1) में कड़े दण्ड के प्रावधान जोड़े गए हैं:
1. धारा 5(m) के अंतर्गत 12 वर्ष से कम आयु के बालक के साथ प्रवेशन लैंगिक हमला किया जाना 'गंभीर प्रकृत प्रवेशन लैंगिक हमला' (Aggravated Penetrative Sexual Assault) माना जाता है।
2. संशोधित धारा 6(1) के अनुसार, जो कोई 12 वर्ष से कम आयु के बालक पर ऐसा अपराध करेगा, उसे न्यूनतम 20 वर्ष के कठोर कारावास (Rigorous Imprisonment) से दण्डित किया जाएगा, जिसे आजीवन कारावास (उस व्यक्ति के प्राकृतिक जीवनकाल के शेष समय तक) अथवा मृत्युदण्ड तक बढ़ाया जा सकता है, तथा वह जुर्माने का भी दायी होगा।

2019 के संशोधन से पूर्व इस अपराध के लिए न्यूनतम सजा 10 वर्ष थी, जिसे बढ़ाकर कम से कम 20 वर्ष किया गया है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (C) 20 years rigorous imprisonment

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: The 2019 statutory amendments inserted Section 5(m) and Section 6(1), prescribing enhanced penalties for penetrative sexual assault on a child below twelve years of age. Reason (R) is true: The government indeed promotes education and assists employees by reimbursing tuition fees and educational expenses under service rules.
Thus, (A) is false, but (R) is true.

questions.explanation_english: The 81st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2000 introduced Clause (4B) into Article 16 of the Constitution of India to address the issue of unfilled reserved vacancies. Article 16(4B) provides that unfilled reserved vacancies of a recruitment year which are carried forward to the succeeding year or years ('backlog vacancies') shall be treated as a distinct and separate class of vacancies. questions.explanation_english: Section 3(1) of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016 strictly prohibits discrimination against any person with disability on the ground of disability, unless it is shown that the impugned act or omission is a 'proportionate means of achieving a legitimate aim'. The law imposes a rigorous proportionality test, meaning differential treatment cannot be excused on grounds of administrative convenience, financial incapacity, institutional preferences, or parental consent. Any departure from non-discrimination must serve a legitimate statutory purpose and must be strictly proportionate, ensuring that arbitrary distinctions violate Article 14 of the Constitution.

questions.explanation_english: This constitutes an offence exclusively under the POCSO Act, 2012. The reasons are two-fold: First, the POSH Act, 2013 (Section 2(a)) defines an 'aggrieved woman' and is gender-specific, protecting only women against workplace sexual harassment; it does not extend protection to male victims. Second, the POCSO Act, 2012 is entirely gender-neutral. Under Section 2(1)(d) of the POCSO Act, a 'child' is defined as any person below the age of 18 years, irrespective of sex. Under Section 11/12 (sexual harassment of a child) and Section 9(c) (aggravated sexual assault committed by a teacher or person on the staff of an educational institution having authority or trust over the child), demanding sexual favours from a 16-year-old boy constitutes an aggravated sexual offence under POCSO. As Head of the Institution, the Principal is under a non-derogable statutory duty under Section 19 of the POCSO Act to report the matter immediately to the Special Juvenile Police Unit (SJPU) or the local police, with failure to report attracting criminal prosecution under Section 21.

2. पॉक्सो (POCSO) अधिनियम, 2012 पूर्णतः लिंग-तटस्थ (Gender-neutral) है। धारा 2(1)(d) के अनुसार 'बालक' का अर्थ 18 वर्ष से कम आयु का कोई भी व्यक्ति (बालक अथवा बालिका) है।

questions.question_english: Article 16(4A) of the Constitution empowers the State to provide reservation in matters of promotion in public services. To which specific categories or groups does Article 16(4A) exclusively apply?
options_english: Socially and Educationally Backward Classes (SEBCs / OBCs)
Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes only
Economically Weaker Sections (EWS) of citizens
Persons with Benchmark Disabilities (PwBD)
questions.explanation_english:
Article 16(4A) was introduced into the Constitution by the Constitution (Seventy-Seventh Amendment) Act, 1995, specifically to nullify the effect of the Supreme Court's ruling in Indra Sawhney v. Union of India (1992), wherein the Court had held that reservation under Article 16(4) is confined only to initial/direct appointments and does not extend to promotions.

Parliament enacted Article 16(4A), which provides: 'Nothing in this article shall prevent the State from making any provision for reservation in matters of promotion, with consequential seniority, to any class or classes of posts in the services under the State in favour of the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes which, in the opinion of the State, are not adequately represented in the services under the State.'

Crucially, Article 16(4A) applies EXCLUSIVELY to Scheduled Castes (SC) and Scheduled Tribes (ST). It does not apply to Other Backward Classes (OBCs) or Economically Weaker Sections (EWS). Therefore, reservation in promotion in central/state government employment is constitutionally permissible only for SC and ST categories.
questions.explanation_hindi:
संविधान (77वां संशोधन) अधिनियम, 1995 द्वारा संविधान में अनुच्छेद 16(4A) जोड़ा गया था। इसका मुख्य उद्देश्य 'इंद्रा साहनी बनाम भारत संघ (1992)' मामले में सर्वोच्च न्यायालय के उस निर्णय के प्रभाव को समाप्त करना था, जिसमें न्यायालय ने कहा था कि अनुच्छेद 16(4) के तहत आरक्षण केवल सीधी/प्रारंभिक नियुक्तियों तक सीमित है और पदोन्नति में लागू नहीं हो सकता।

संसद ने अनुच्छेद 16(4A) जोड़कर यह स्पष्ट प्रावधान किया कि राज्य को 'अनुसूचित जातियों और अनुसूचित जनजातियों' के पक्ष में, जिनका राज्य की सेवाओं में पर्याप्त प्रतिनिधित्व नहीं है, पदोन्नति के मामलों में परिणामी वरिष्ठता सहित आरक्षण देने से नहीं रोका जा सकेगा।

महत्वपूर्ण बिंदु यह है कि अनुच्छेद 16(4A) का लाभ विशेष रूप से और केवल 'अनुसूचित जातियों (SC) और अनुसूचित जनजातियों (ST)' पर लागू होता है। यह अन्य पिछड़ा वर्ग (OBC) या आर्थिक रूप से कमजोर वर्ग (EWS) पर लागू नहीं होता है। अतः सरकारी नौकरियों में पदोन्नति में आरक्षण केवल SC और ST संवर्ग के लिए ही संवैधानिक रूप से मान्य है।

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Article 16(4A) was added to the Constitution by the Seventy-Seventh Amendment Act of 1995 to enable reservation in matters of promotion. This specific clause applies exclusively to members of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes, empowering the State to provide promotional reservations with consequential seniority in services under the State's administrative control.
